bib.title: FACTSCORE: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation

question: How can the factual precision of long-form LM generations be measured at fine granularity, by humans and automatically?
hypothesis: Atomic facts scored against a given knowledge source give a finer, more informative precision measure than binary or sentence-level judgments, and retrieval plus a strong LM can estimate it closely.
contributions: FACTSCORE: fraction of atomic facts supported by a given knowledge source, with human evaluation of InstructGPT, ChatGPT and PerplexityAI
An automatic estimator of FACTSCORE with error rate under 2%
Open-sourced FACTSCORE and annotated data (pip install factscore)

method.summary: Generations are split into atomic facts (InstructGPT few-shot, human-revised) and each is labelled Supported, Not-supported or Irrelevant against English Wikipedia; FACTSCORE is the fraction supported. An estimator retrieves passages (GTR) and asks an LM True or False, optionally ensembled with a nonparametric masked-LM probability, and is applied to 13 subjects.
method.task: Factual precision evaluation of long-form biography generation

datasets.name: Human-annotated biographies
datasets.size: 183 people entities x 3 LMs (InstructGPT, ChatGPT, PerplexityAI)
datasets.split: entities sampled uniformly over 20 categories (5 frequency x 4 nationality)
datasets.source: Wikidata entities with Wikipedia pages; annotated by Upwork freelancers

datasets.name: Unlabeled biographies for 13 subjects
datasets.split: no entity overlap with the 183 annotated entities
datasets.source: 12 LMs plus human-written bios from DBPedia (unavailable for 11% of entities, counted as abstain)

datasets.name: English Wikipedia (knowledge source)
datasets.preprocessing: pages split into passages up to 256 tokens; retrieval restricted to topic entity's page

models.name: GPT-4, Alpaca 7B/13B/65B, Vicuna 7B/13B, Dolly 12B, Oasst-pythia 12B, StableLM-tuned-alpha 7B, MPT Chat 7B
Inst-LLAMA 7B (LLAMA 7B trained on Super Natural Instructions)

inference.samples: One generation per entity per subject; 500 entities for new LMs; Fig 5 resampling: N in {40,100,200} of 500, M=100 repeats
inference.prompting: Subject prompt 'Tell me a bio of <entity>'. Evaluator: zero-shot '<atomic-fact> True or False?' with retrieved passages prepended for Retrieve->LM; prediction compares logits of True/False, or checks generated text for True/False when logits unavailable (ChatGPT). Atomic fact generation uses 8 few-shot exemplars on InstructGPT (Table 15).
inference.retrieval: GTR large, restricted to topic entity's Wikipedia page, k=5 passages, up to 256 tokens each (k=3 for editing)

parameters.evaluator_variants: No-context LM, Retrieve->LM, NP, Retrieve->LM + NP (Supported only if both agree)

metrics.name: FACTSCORE
metrics.definition: f(y)=1/|Ay| sum over atomic facts of I[a supported by C]; averaged over prompts where model responds

metrics.name: Error Rate (ER)
metrics.definition: difference between ground-truth and estimated FACTSCORE (sign shown by +/- over 5% over/under-estimation)

metrics.name: F1micro
metrics.definition: F1 for detecting Not-supported atomic facts with oracle atomic facts, per-fact decisions

metrics.name: ErrLoc / EditCorr(ErrCorr) / SimAl
metrics.definition: Editing metrics: token preservation macro-F1; token F1 of added tokens vs gold edit; normalized SIM paraphrase similarity

eval.protocol: Human labels from fact-checking freelancers (2-hour qualification, 10% of HITs double-annotated; agreement 96/90/88%); estimator compared against human FACTSCORE by ER and ranking preservation across 3 subjects; variance by 100 random subsets

prompts.text: concatenation of k retrieved passages, the atomic fact, and 'True or False?'
Please breakdown the following sentence into independent facts: <sentence> followed by 8 exemplars (Table 15)

limits: Only people biographies and English Wikipedia; NLP-paper proof of concept is 10 prompts
Assumes undebatable, equal-weight, non-conflicting facts; 70% of annotator disagreements were inherent debatability
Precision only: no recall, abstention and fewer facts raise the score; authors recommend reporting abstention rate and facts per response
Estimator is not perfect on individual judgments and best variant depends on the subject
Wikipedia coverage gaps penalize true facts (3 of 30 checked)
Human results on only 183 entities per model; pre-2023 models and commercial systems
